title: Core ItemSources reverse index and drop-rate computation (moved from ContentValidator.World.cs)
player_outcome: No visible change on its own. It gives the Guide book exact 'Obtained from' data (drops with percentages, shops, chests, crafting, fishing, crates) and makes the content validator use the same index.
design: Verified: the item-source enumeration exists only inside ContentValidator.ValidateObtainability (ContentValidator.World.cs:241-273); it produces a HashSet with no owners or rates.

New Content/Index/ItemSources.cs: ItemSourceIndex Build(ContentDatabase). A source is ItemSource(Kind, ContentDef? Owner, string? Label, float? Chance, int Min, int Max, TypedSpec[] Conditions). Kinds: Recipe, Drop (enemy loot), BossDrop, Container (chest tables named by the table's Name), Object (tile object Loot or natural placing item), Block (BlockDrops), Catch (critter CatchItem), Shop (town NPC + tab + conditions + currency), VisitorPool, Fishing (the 'fishing' table, ProjectileSystem.FishingTable), Opened (items whose consume behaviour names a loot table, from ItemUseSystem.cs:274), AnglerReward, DyeTrade, Bucket, Tag (starter/world).
Loot owners: resolve table → enemies/objects/items/fishing. Nested tables inherit the owner, with the chance multiplied through DropRates.

New Gameplay/Loot/DropRates.cs: For(ContentDatabase, tableId) → List<DropInfo(ItemDef Item, float Chance, int Min, int Max, TypedSpec[] Conditions)>. Each-mode entries: chance. Weighted: 1 - (1 - w/total)^rolls, computed over entries treated as eligible. Nested: multiplied. Coins reported separately (table.Coins or enemy Value ±25%). Deterministic, pure and thread-safe, so it can be built off the main thread.
ContentValidator.ValidateObtainability becomes a loop over index.HasSource(item) with the same tag exemptions and warning text.

Label chest tables: add 'name' to the loot tables used by world generation (cabin_chest 'Cabin Chests', gold_chest 'Gold Chests', surface_chest 'Surface Chests', sky_chest 'Skyware Chests', temple_chest 'Lihzahrd Chests', pot 'Pots').
tests: ItemSourcesTests.ParityWithOldValidator: the set of items with ≥1 source equals the old algorithm's set, with the old code copied into the test as the oracle
ItemSourcesTests: gel has a Drop source from slimes with a chance; torch has Recipe and Shop(merchant); water_bucket has Bucket; leather_whip has Shop(zoologist) after P5-17
DropRatesTests: an each-mode entry at 0.33 gives 0.33; a weighted table with 2 rolls over 4 equal entries gives 1-(0.75)^2; nested table multiplication; coins range
verification: dotnet test; Strata.Tools validate gives the same warnings as before (diff the output)
risks: Conditional entries in weighted tables make the exact rate context-dependent; show the conditions next to the rate.
